questions.title: Implementation plan
questions.text: Describe what a **system implementation plan** is.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A document describing how / when / by whom the new system will be installed and put into use (1)
- listing tasks, order, dates, responsibilities, resources / risks (1)
scheme.model_answer: A document that describes how the new system will be installed and introduced, listing every task with its dates and the person responsible.

questions.title: Why plan
questions.text: Explain the importance of making a system implementation plan.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): no task forgotten; correct order / dependencies; on time — deadlines; responsibilities clear; budget / resources controlled; risks reduced / contingency; minimal disruption; progress monitored
scheme.model_answer: It makes sure every task, such as data conversion and training, is done in the right order and on time, and that there is a backup plan if the new system fails.

questions.title: Elements of the plan
questions.text: The system implementation plan specifies the method of implementing the new system. State **two** more elements that are described in this plan.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): training method for personnel; timing of staff training; plan for installing the application / hardware; data conversion; schedule / timetable; responsible persons; testing; budget / resources; risks / contingency; support / documentation
scheme.model_answer: 1 The training method for staff. 2 The timing of staff training.

questions.title: Plan contents
questions.text: Select **two** items that belong in a system implementation plan.

options.content: How data will be transferred from the old system
The source code of every program
The dates on which staff will be trained

scheme.mark_scheme: A and C. One mark each; a mark is lost for each incorrect option selected.

questions.title: Training methods
questions.text: Match each training method to an advantage.

right.text: Questions are answered immediately and many staff are trained at once
Staff learn at any time and at their own pace
Training matches the needs of each person

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: When to train
questions.text: Explain why staff training should be scheduled **before** the new system goes live.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Staff know how to use the system from the first day (1)
- fewer mistakes / no delays / no loss of data or customers when it starts (1)
scheme.model_answer: Then staff can use the system correctly from the first day, so they do not make mistakes or slow down the work when it goes live.

questions.title: Data conversion
questions.text: Describe **two** methods of converting data from an old system to a new one.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): manual entry of paper records; import / export from old files (CSV, SQL); conversion program changes the format
scheme.model_answer: 1 Typing the data from the paper records into the new system. 2 Exporting the old database to a CSV file and importing it into the new database.

questions.title: Checking converted data
questions.text: Explain why converted data should be **verified**, and describe one way to do it.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Errors can be made when typing / copying data (1)
- verify by double entry / visual check against the original / comparing record counts or totals (1)
scheme.model_answer: Mistakes can be made when the data is typed in, so it is checked by comparing the new records with the original paper records.

questions.title: Backup before conversion
questions.text: A full backup of the old data should be made before data conversion begins.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.
scheme.explanation: If the conversion fails, the original data can be restored.

questions.title: Contingency plan
questions.text: Explain what a **contingency plan** is in system implementation and give an example.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A plan of what to do if something goes wrong / risks (1)
- e.g. return to the old system / restore from backup if the new system fails (1)
scheme.model_answer: A plan for what to do if something goes wrong, for example returning to the old system and restoring the backup if the new system crashes.

questions.title: Order the tasks
questions.text: Number the tasks **1–5** in the order in which they should be carried out.

prefill: Train staff to use the new system
Install the software and create user accounts

scheme.mark_scheme:
Back up 1; install hardware 2; install software 3; train staff 4; start using 5
Five correct (4); four (3); three (2); two (1)
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept backup and hardware installation in either order (1 and 2).

questions.title: Gantt chart
questions.text: Explain why a Gantt chart is useful in an implementation plan.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Shows each task against time — start, end, duration (1)
- shows order / overlap / dependencies so progress can be monitored and deadlines met (1)
scheme.model_answer: It shows every task as a bar on a timeline, so the manager can see which tasks overlap, which must finish first, and whether the project is on schedule.

questions.title: A restaurant system
questions.text: A restaurant is replacing paper orders with tablets for waiters and a screen in the kitchen. It is open every day from 10:00 to 23:00.

parts.title: Timing
parts.text: Suggest when the hardware should be installed and justify your answer.

scheme.mark_scheme: Outside opening hours / at night / on a quiet day (1); so that service is not disrupted (1)
scheme.model_answer: At night after 23:00, so the installation does not disturb customers or waiters.

parts.title: Training
parts.text: Suggest a suitable training method for the waiters and justify it.

scheme.mark_scheme: Method (1) + justification linked to waiters / restaurant (1), e.g. short hands-on group session before opening — practise on the real tablets
scheme.model_answer: A short hands-on group session on the tablets before opening, so all waiters practise taking orders together and can ask questions.

parts.title: Contingency
parts.text: Suggest **one** item for the contingency plan.

scheme.mark_scheme: Risk (1) + action (1), e.g. tablets / Wi-Fi fail → keep paper order pads available
scheme.model_answer: If the Wi-Fi or tablets stop working, waiters go back to paper order pads, which are kept at the bar.

questions.title: Write an implementation plan
questions.text: A school is replacing its paper attendance registers with an online attendance system used by 60 teachers. Make a system implementation plan. Include the method, the main tasks in order with responsibilities, data conversion, training and a contingency measure.

scheme.mark_scheme: One mark each (max 6): justified method (e.g. pilot in one grade / parallel); hardware / software installation and accounts; data conversion of student lists + verification; training method and timing for teachers; tasks in a sensible order with responsible people / dates; testing before go-live; contingency (keep paper registers / backup); review / support
scheme.model_answer: Method: pilot in Grade 7 for two weeks, then the whole school. 1 IT technician sets up the server and accounts for 60 teachers (week 1). 2 Office staff import the class lists from the existing spreadsheet and check them against the paper registers (week 1–2). 3 Teachers attend a one-hour training session and receive a quick guide (week 2). 4 Acceptance test with test data (week 2). 5 Pilot in Grade 7 while paper registers are kept (weeks 3–4). 6 Whole-school go-live (week 5). Contingency: paper registers are kept for one term and the database is backed up every night. A review meeting is held after one month.

questions.title: The implementation plan
questions.text: A clinic has a new electronic patient-record system ready and is preparing its system implementation plan.

parts.title: Importance
parts.text: Explain the importance of making a system implementation plan.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): tasks in order / none forgotten; on time; responsibilities; risks reduced / contingency; minimal disruption; budget
scheme.model_answer: It makes sure every task is done in the correct order by the right person, so the clinic can keep treating patients during the changeover and data is not lost.

parts.title: Elements
parts.text: The plan specifies the method of implementing the new system. State **two** more elements that are described in this plan.

scheme.mark_scheme: Determine the training method for personnel (1); determine the timing of staff training (1); plan for the installation of the application (1); data conversion; schedule; responsibilities; contingency [Max 2]
scheme.model_answer: 1 The training method for the staff. 2 The plan for installing the application.

parts.title: Training methods
parts.text: Draw a line to link each training method to its disadvantage.

right.text: All staff must leave their work at the same time
No one is available to answer questions immediately
Expensive and slow when many staff need training

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3. One mark per line.

parts.title: Risk
parts.text: State **one** problem that could occur if the clinic implements the system without a plan.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any one (1): staff not trained; data lost / incorrect; deadline missed; no backup; over budget; disruption to patients
scheme.model_answer: Patient records could be lost during data conversion.

questions.title: Data conversion
questions.text: The clinic has 4 000 patient records: some on paper cards and some in an old spreadsheet.

parts.title: Methods
parts.text: Describe how each type of record could be transferred to the new system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Paper cards: manual data entry / typing in (1)
Spreadsheet: export (e.g. CSV) and import into the new database (1)
scheme.model_answer: Paper cards: staff type the details into the new system. Spreadsheet: save it as a CSV file and import it into the new database.

parts.title: Verification
parts.text: Explain why the converted records must be verified.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Typing / import errors may occur (1)
- wrong medical data could harm patients / the system must start with accurate data (1)
scheme.model_answer: Mistakes can happen when 4 000 records are typed or imported, and a wrong allergy or date of birth could harm a patient, so the data must match the originals.

parts.title: Backup
parts.text: Explain why a backup should be made before the conversion starts.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Conversion may fail / corrupt / lose data (1)
- the original data can be restored from the backup (1)
scheme.model_answer: If the import goes wrong and damages the data, the original records can be restored from the backup.

parts.title: Contingency
parts.text: Suggest **one** contingency measure in case the new system fails on its first day.

scheme.mark_scheme: Measure (1) + explanation (1): keep old system / paper cards available (parallel); restore backup; developer on call
scheme.model_answer: Keep the paper cards and old spreadsheet in use until the new system is proven, so doctors can still see patient details.

questions.title: Making the plan
questions.text: The project manager lists the tasks for the clinic's implementation plan.

parts.title: Order
parts.text: Number the tasks **1–5** in the order they should be done.

prefill: Install the computers in the consulting rooms
Install the software and create user accounts
Go live with the new system

scheme.mark_scheme:
Install computers 1; install software 2; convert records 3; train staff 4; go live 5
Accept training as 3 and conversion as 4.
Five correct (4); four (3); three (2); two (1)
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept conversion and training in either order (3 and 4).

parts.title: Training first
parts.text: Explain why training must be completed before the clinic goes live.

scheme.mark_scheme: Staff can use the system correctly from day one (1); avoids errors / delays with patients (1)
scheme.model_answer: So doctors and receptionists can use it correctly from the first day and patients are not delayed by mistakes.

parts.title: Gantt chart
parts.text: The plan is shown as a Gantt chart. State **two** things a Gantt chart shows.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): the tasks; start and end dates / duration; order / overlap of tasks; milestones; progress / responsible person
scheme.model_answer: 1 The start and end date of each task. 2 Which tasks overlap.

summary: Why a system implementation plan is important, what it contains (method, schedule, hardware and software installation, data conversion, staff training, testing, responsibilities, risks and support), and how to make an implementation plan with a timeline for a new system.

blocks.content: A document that describes **how, when and by whom** a new system will be **installed and put into use**, replacing the old system. It lists **every task**, its **order**, **dates**, the **people responsible**, the **resources** needed and what to do **if something goes wrong**.

Implementing a new system involves many people (developers, managers, staff, suppliers) and many tasks that depend on each other: the hardware must be installed before the software, the data must be converted before the system goes live, staff must be trained before they use it. Without a plan, tasks are forgotten, done in the wrong order or late.

items.title: Why the plan is important
items.content:
- Makes sure **no task is forgotten** (data conversion, training, backups).
- Puts tasks in the **correct order** and shows **dependencies**.
- Sets **deadlines** so the system goes live **on time**.
- Gives each task a **responsible person** — everyone knows their role.
- Controls the **budget** and **resources** (equipment, staff time, trainers).
- **Reduces risk**: plans a **backup** and what to do if the new system fails (contingency).
- **Minimises disruption** to the organisation's normal work (e.g. installing at weekends).
- Allows managers to **monitor progress** and check the implementation was successful.

items.title: What can go wrong without a plan
items.content:
- Staff are **not trained** when the system starts, so mistakes are made.
- **Data is lost** or entered incorrectly during conversion.
- Hardware arrives **late**, so the go-live date is missed.
- No **backup** of the old system — the business stops if the new one fails.
- Costs run **over budget**.

blocks.title: Elements of a system implementation plan
rows: **Implementation method**
Direct, parallel, pilot or phased — and why it was chosen
**Schedule / timetable**
The tasks, their **start and end dates**, their order and **milestones** (often a Gantt chart)
**Hardware installation**
What equipment is bought and installed, where, and when (computers, servers, network, scanners)
**Software installation**
Installing and configuring the application, OS, database; setting up **user accounts and access rights**
**Data conversion (migration)**
How data is **transferred** from the old system (manual entry, import from files), and how it is **checked** (verification)
**Staff training**
**Who** is trained, the **training method**, the **timing** of training, who runs it
**Testing before go-live**
Final **acceptance testing** with the client; checking converted data
**Responsibilities**
The person or team responsible for each task
**Resources and budget**
Equipment, staff time, trainers, costs
**Risks and contingency plan**
What could go wrong and what to do (backup of the old data, rollback to the old system)
**Documentation and support**
User guide, technical documentation, help desk after go-live
**Review / evaluation**
How and when the success of the implementation will be checked

blocks.title: Staff training methods
rows: **Classroom / group sessions** with a trainer
Questions answered immediately; many staff at once
Staff away from work; one pace for all
**One-to-one training**
Matches the learner's needs
Expensive, slow for many staff
**Online courses / video tutorials**
Any time, at the learner's own pace; cheap to repeat
No immediate help; staff may skip it
**User manuals / quick guides**
Always available for reference
Some people do not read them
**"Train the trainer"** — key users train colleagues
Cheaper; trainers know the workplace
Quality depends on the key users
**Practice / training mode of the system**
Hands-on with realistic data, no risk
Takes time to set up

blocks.title: Data conversion methods
rows: **Manual entry** — typing data from paper records
Old system was paper-based
**Verification**: double entry / visual check
**Import / export** — data copied from old files into the new database (CSV, SQL scripts)
Old system was computerised
Compare record counts and totals; sample checks
**Conversion program** written to change the format
Old and new formats are very different
Test the program on a copy first

blocks.content: Always make a **full backup of the old data** before conversion begins, so nothing is lost if the conversion fails.

blocks.title: How to write the plan
items: Choose the **implementation method** and justify it.
List **all tasks**: hardware, software, accounts, data conversion, training, testing, go-live, support, review.
Put the tasks in **order** and note which depend on others.
Estimate the **duration** of each task and set **dates** and **milestones**.
Assign a **responsible person** to each task.
Show the plan as a **table** and a **Gantt chart**.

blocks.title: Contingency plan
rows: The new system crashes during parallel running
Continue with the paper system; developer fixes the fault

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: The system implementation plan specifies the method of implementing the new system. State two more elements that are described in this plan. [2]**
Determine the **training method** for personnel (1); determine the **timing of staff training** / plan for **installation of the application** / **data conversion** / **schedule** / **responsible persons** (1).

**Q: Explain the importance of making a system implementation plan. [2]**
It makes sure all tasks — installation, data conversion, training — are done in the **correct order and on time** (1), so the changeover causes **little disruption** and **risks** such as data loss are reduced (1).

**Q: Explain why data should be verified after conversion. [2]**
Errors can be made when **copying or typing** the data into the new system (1); verification (double entry / comparing with the original) ensures the new system starts with **accurate data** (1).

- Listing only the **method** — the plan also covers schedule, installation, data conversion, training, testing and contingency.
- Training staff **after** the system goes live.
- Forgetting to **back up** the old data before conversion.
- A plan without **dates** or **responsible people**.

items: Give four reasons why an implementation plan is important.
